primary_claim: In weak-judge/strong-debater experiments on coding (BigCodeBench+) and reasoning (ARC-AGI) tasks with verifiable ground truth, generative debate underperforms consultancy in 11 of 16 conditions, and stripping debate transcripts entirely (showing the judge only proposed answers) matches or outperforms both, because judges default to endorsing plausible-sounding arguments when both debaters are wrong and debate transcripts amplify this false-positive tendency (e.g. 90% FPR under debate vs 30% no-transcript baseline on BCB+).

effect.metric: judge verdict accuracy; false positive rate (FPR)
effect.value: debate loses to consultancy in 11/16 conditions, ties in 4, wins in 1 (+5.1pp, p<0.01); dual proposer debate FPR 90% vs 30% no-transcript baseline (BCB+, GPT-5); both-wrong regime verdict accuracy 11% (debate) vs 62% (consultancy), a 50.5pp gap

contradicts_or_qualifies: Irving et al. (2018)'s AI Debate proposal for scalable oversight, which predicts adversarial argument should surface truth for the judge; authors find this advantage does not materialize at inference time with current models even in a more natural generative (non-assigned-sides) framing

Prior debate literature showing an advantage in information-constrained settings; authors note (per prior work) this advantage disappears when the judge has full context access, the more relevant condition for AI-to-AI oversight
stated_future_work: Debater training via RL targeting solution quality directly, not just speech quality
Multi-turn settings allowing deeper engagement between debaters
Judge training and debiasing, if judge capability is the binding constraint
Competitive settings where debaters are assigned sides or incentivized to disagree
limitations_stated: Results should be interpreted through the lens of dataset saturation: GPT-5 is near ceiling on BCB+, leaving little room for formats to differentiate
Best-of-4 gains are generally insufficient to close the accuracy gap between debate and consultancy
Speech-time best-of-N is a loose proxy for RL training since it cannot change the solutions themselves
Judge side bias (a 'both correct' bias) may be a confound not fully disentangled from content-based judging
quote: The core mechanism is that judges default to endorsing plausible-sounding arguments when both participants are wrong, and debate transcripts specifically amplify this tendency.
